title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield spiked to a 24-year intraday high near 5.34% before easing to close at 5.233%, while French, Italian and Greek bond yields jumped in a chaotic selloff across European sovereign debt.

Markets: Wall Street recovered from early losses as the S&P 500 rose 0.2% and the Nasdaq finished roughly flat; crude oil jumped 2.7% to ~$92.87/bbl on renewed Iran tensions after reports the U.S. is sending a third aircraft carrier to the Middle East.
Markets: 30-year fixed mortgage rates leapt to 7.28% from 7.03% (Freddie Mac) — the biggest one-week jump since 2022 — as the bond-market selloff spills into the housing market.

Macro/Policy: Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson signaled officials need more time before deciding on further rate hikes, even as ISM manufacturing data came in slightly soft but showed a jump in prices paid by producers.
Macro/Policy: All eyes turn to Friday's September jobs report, the next major data point shaping the Fed's rate path.
Companies: Google unveiled its long-awaited Gemini 4 Argon model, claiming it beats OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra on several coding and knowledge benchmarks after a long gap atop its model lineup.
Companies: The FTC is investigating OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI firms over safety risks, while Apple is reportedly readying a home hub device for an Oct. 13 launch.
